svg.title: The example conversation: expenses recorded in plain language, balances updating, and the final settlement.

div.div: I booked the apartment in Le Marais, €690 for the three of us — me, Brand and Cooper

div.p: Got it — €690 split three ways is €230 each, and you fronted the whole thing.

div.div: Brand paid this one. Cooper didn't drink though — the wine's just me and Brand.

div.p: Dinner came to €124.00. Taking the €32.00 Chinon off the top for you and Brand (€16.00 each), the remaining €92.00 splits three ways, with Brand out of pocket for the whole €124.00.

div.div: Doyle got in on Thursday and booked the Seine dinner cruise — €280 for the four of us

div.p: Doyle's in — €280 four ways is €70 each, and Doyle covered it.

div.div: Brand sat out the Louvre — €66, just me, Cooper and Doyle. I paid.

div.p: €66 three ways is €22 each for you, Cooper and Doyle, on your card.

div.div: Coop got the taxi to CDG, €56 — split it four ways

div.p: €56 four ways is €14 each, with Cooper paying.

div.div: oh — the cruise was €300, not €280. Doyle just forwarded the confirmation.

div.p: Updated the cruise to €300 — €75 each instead of €70.

div.div: Cooper gave me €100 in cash this morning

div.p: Balances stay as they are until you tell me the payments have actually gone through.
